So, LCPS's open enrollment period is October 15th through November 15th. Every benefits-eligible employee should have received the 2024 Open Enrollment Guide in the mail last week. Information about changes, updates, and enhancements are provided in this document, as well as the new rates for health insurance as of 2025.

LCPS offers a wide variety of voluntary benefits. These are benefits for which the employee will pay a premium or contribution, as well as benefits for which an employee might be automatically enrolled, meaning they're not having to do anything to be enrolled, and they're not necessarily making a premium or contribution.

We have three health insurance programs, the High Deductible Health Plan, or the HDHP, the Open Access Plus, or the OAP, and then the new one this year, the Open Access High Plan, which is replacing the Point of Service Plan. Under the High Deductible Plan, LCPS contributes to a health savings account to help pay for medical expenses.

Employees can also contribute to this plan tax-free, and HSA funds can be used to help offset medical expenses. An HSA can roll over from year to year and can be invested in a stock market plan if the employee so chooses.

All employees, regardless of whether they're enrolled in LCPS Health Insurance, can contribute to a flexible spending account. So we have two different flexible spending accounts, dependent care and medical. FSAs must be spent within the plan year, although there is often a grace period allowed for an extra few months if you didn't spend all your medical or your dependent care.

They also have a small carryover that we are currently permitting can be carried over from year to year. These are the only programs that an employee has to re-enroll in every year if they want to participate. The IRS sets the limits on these plans, the amount that can be contributed to both an FSA and an HSA.

But I also wanted to talk about some of the voluntary benefits that are not health insurance. We offer an accidental injury insurance plan and a critical illness plan. These plans are very affordable, and we encourage everyone who is eligible to take a hard look at these programs.

Under the Accidental Injury Plan, if a covered individual were to have an accident that requires care through an urgent care emergency room, the employee receives a financial benefit and actual check to help cover the copay for that care. Follow-up care, including possible surgical or physical therapy, is also covered under this insurance.

There are two different levels for this plan, and details about each level are available on the Employee Benefits website, or you can contact Cigna directly for additional information. Premiums for this plan range from $2.05 a paycheck to $11.71 a paycheck.

The Critical Illness Plan provides a cash benefit to covered individuals who are diagnosed with a covered critical illness. The coverage ranges from $5,000 up to $25,000 for a covered illness. Employees who are enrolled in the HDHP plan are automatically enrolled in a $5,000 critical illness plan.

And they have the option of adding an additional $20,000, bringing them up to that $25,000 maximum. This is a cash benefit, helping an employee when they or a covered family member are facing a significant illness to help meet their financial obligations.

And the point of service plan has been moved to the open access high plan or the OAP high. The change from POS to the OAP High, bless you, allows employees to access care without a referral from their primary care provider.

This is the only significant change in the plan. The plan design, the deductibles, and the co-pays remain the same as they were in the POS, but instead of a local network of in-network providers specifically designed for LCPS, employees are now able to access providers in-network nationwide.

This change provides easier access for employees and their family members to care wherever they are and it allows all of the LCPS plans under Cigna to be on one platform, which helps save us a little bit of money.

The IRS also initiated a change this year for the employees enrolled in the high deductible plan. The plan deductible is increasing $50 for the individual and $100 for the employee plus one or more. This is not an LCPS increase, but one that is regulated by the IRS.

The new deductibles are $1,650 for the individual and $3,300 for the employee plus one or more. As part of the budget process last year, an 8% increase in health insurance premiums was approved and will take effect on January 1, 2025.
